why: XLRE +1.96 pct to $41.61, first up week after seven down, closing over the $41.33 shelf after trading to $40.28 Thursday (28 cents from the $40.00 objective); the 20D $41.64 is three cents overhead and the 200D/trapdoor $42.50-42.57 is the target where Marky takes the position down (wiki/real-estate.md; macro/facts.json).

The week's engine was three tower stocks on a tenant that has not signed: AMT +12.4, SBAC +15.1, CCI +19.9 pct on SpaceX's reported $8B spectrum purchase -- roughly 0.7 of the fund's 2.0 points was AMT alone and the staged top-two contribution is 74.8 pct, the highest on the board; WELL, VTR and SPG fell; EQIX and DLR did nothing (wiki/real-estate.md; wiki/synthesis.md Wire 3; inputs/2026-10-09/real_estate.json metrics).

The fundamental case did not improve: the 30-year mortgage 7.40 pct (second weekly rise), Trepp CMBS delinquency 8.02 pct (multifamily 8.04, office 12.16), carry gap -171bp; Ophelia's relief condition (a lower weekly 10Y close) was met by three basis points -- 'not enough and not nothing'; stance avoid -> watch, no new duration (wiki/real-estate.md Ophelia; wiki/synthesis.md Section 4).

Week RF raised 20 -> 25 and MC 35 -> 42: CPI Wed is the direct test and Prologis Thu Oct 15 (company-confirmed) is the first REIT print into depressed positioning, 'where an in-line quarter is enough' (wiki/real-estate.md Marky; wiki/earnings-surveillance.md).
risks: The tower rally unwinds: spectrum is not a lease, approval can slip, carriers can respond; if it fades the fund gives back roughly a third of the week (wiki/real-estate.md RISK SCENARIOS and WILD CARD).
Falsifier: a close under $40.57 (Wednesday's low close) makes $40.28 and $40.00 live; the 10Y takes out 5.364 pct and the 30Y 5.63 pct (wiki/real-estate.md).

Bullish falsifier: a second lower weekly 10Y close -- Cecil buys O (6.0 pct, RSI 32) first, then WELL; Ophelia says 'the term premium turned'; a close over $42.57 ends the downtrend (wiki/real-estate.md Cecil; wiki/synthesis.md Section 5).

OWNER OPTION: the 74.8 pct top-two concentration is a quality concern the arithmetic does not see; prior cycles left coverage warnings at risk_penalty 0.0 and no cycle has applied a concentration penalty. A 0.02 penalty here would move the week score from 45.1 (neutral) to 43.1 (unfavorable). This proposal leaves it at 0.0 for consistency and flags the border.

why: Month arithmetic is the second-worst on the board (breadth 11.1, relative momentum 10, up-volume 27.8 pct, -5.36 pts vs SPY) and XLRE's correlation to SPY fell most of any sector (0.737 -> 0.569) -- it uncoupled by outperforming on a headline (wiki/canary-watch.md SECTOR CORRELATION MATRIX; inputs/2026-10-09/real_estate.json metrics).

Calendar-page Ophelia: REITs 'need a core print at or below +0.2 pct to hold'; the 10Y is 5.244 pct with 5.364 pct overhead and the Fed will hike again by year-end -- the regime is the one the sector has lost to for four weekly closes under its 200D (wiki/economic-calendar.md COUNCIL READ; wiki/real-estate.md TECHNICAL LEVELS).

Month RF raised 20 -> 25 and MC 42 -> 45: PLD Oct 15, GTY/CCI Oct 21, CBRE Oct 22, WELL/PSA Oct 26, AMT/VTR Oct 27, EQIX Oct 28, DLR Oct 29, O/SBAC Nov 2, SPG Nov 5; FOMC Oct 27-28; Trepp's October report in early November (wiki/real-estate.md EARNINGS CALENDAR).
risks: Labor weakness arrives as tenant weakness before it arrives as lower yields; a CRE default headline in the Q4 maturity stack at 7 pct+ refinancing costs; multifamily delinquency already above the overall rate (wiki/real-estate.md RISK SCENARIOS).

No data-center leasing announcement was found this month; EQIX and DLR were flat while the AI loop paid the utilities -- the one link in Wire 2 that did not fire (wiki/synthesis.md Wire 2; wiki/real-estate.md).

Bullish falsifier: 'a 3.53 pct yield 171bp under the risk-free rate, at an RSI that was 25.7 a week ago, is the position from which this asset class has produced its sharpest rallies -- and they begin without warning' (wiki/real-estate.md WILD CARD).

extracts.lead_summary: The magnet let go. XLRE traded as low as $40.28 on Thursday — twelve cents under last week's low and twenty-eight cents from the $40.00 objective — and then closed Friday at $41.61 (+1.9% on the day, +2.0% on the week), over the $41.33 shelf I told you would be the first sign the move was done. It is the first up week after seven down. The reason was not the one I named: the 10-year closed 5.24%, three basis points lower, but the week's engine was a single Thursday-night headline — SpaceX buying $8 billion of 800 MHz spectrum — that sent American Tower +12.4%, SBA +15.1% and Crown Castle +19.9% in one session. The mortgage rate went the other way, to 7.40%. The towers do not make a sector low; I am watching whether anything else confirms it.
